qualifying_findings.title: Google MCP Toolbox allowedLocalRoots symlink boundary bypass
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD describes improper symlink resolution in Google MCP Toolbox for Databases versions 1.2.0 through 1.9.0. A remote authenticated attacker with tool execution permissions can bypass allowedLocalRoots directory restrictions and access or overwrite local files outside permitted roots.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database with linked vendor pull request
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Google MCP Toolbox for Databases 1.2.0 through 1.9.0; local filesystem root enforcement for MCP database tools
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP database tools often bridge AI agents to local data and files; path-boundary bypass turns delegated tool execution into broader filesystem read/write authority.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: General Google and MCP Toolbox product context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General database-agent workflow selection is development-practice-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Owns the symlink root bypass, affected versions, delegated tool authority, and local-file security implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for date, affected range, and security boundary from NVD; ingest should recheck the merged/fixed release once vendor release notes are visible.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, verify whether a release after 1.9.0 contains PR 3810.
Consider a local leaf under agent-and-tool-security or data-and-privacy depending on whether the primary impact is tool authority or file exposure.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenClaw mcp.app.view read-to-write authorization bypass
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD reports that OpenClaw before 2026.9.4 lets read-scoped operators obtain and redeem a standalone ticket through mcp.app.view to invoke MCP App tools that require operator.write scope.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database with vendor release, commit, and advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenClaw before 2026.9.4; MCP App standalone ticket authorization path
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The flaw crosses read/write delegated-authority boundaries for AI/MCP app tools, allowing state-changing agent actions from lower-privilege credentials.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: General OpenClaw product context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent workflow implications are development-practice-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Owns the read-to-write authorization bypass, release boundary, and delegated authority risk.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD plus vendor and commit references; prior OpenClaw security leaves exist, so ingest should decide whether this updates a cluster or needs a new leaf.
follow_up_actions: Delta-review against existing OpenClaw authorization leaves.
Verify release 2026.9.4 remediation wording before durable synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: mcp-chrome-bridge CORS origin bypass exposes browser automation tools
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD describes an origin validation error in mcp-chrome-bridge through 1.0.31. Malicious pages can make cross-origin requests to the local native-server HTTP API and invoke browser automation tools, including script execution, page-content reading, and screenshot capture.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database with project issue and advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-chrome-bridge through 1.0.31; local browser automation HTTP API
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Browser MCP bridges are high-risk delegated-action surfaces; CORS/origin bypass lets untrusted web content drive local browser tools and potentially read or manipulate session context.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: General mcp-chrome project catalog context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General browser-agent runtime practice is development-practice-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Owns the CORS origin bypass, local browser tool exposure, and delegated browser authority risk.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for vulnerability presence and affected version from NVD; fixed-version status is not visible in the captured NVD references.
follow_up_actions: Recheck project issue 384 for remediation status during ingest.
Route to an agent/browser tool security leaf if not already covered.

qualifying_findings.title: mark3labs mcp-filesystem-server dangling-symlink traversal
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD reports that mark3labs mcp-filesystem-server v0.11.1 mishandles dangling symlinks in validatePath. File-writing tools can follow a symlink inside an allowed directory and create or modify files outside configured allowed directories.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database with security advisory reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mark3labs mcp-filesystem-server v0.11.1; write_file, modify_file, copy_file, move_file, and create_directory path validation
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Filesystem MCP servers are direct agent-to-host mutation channels; symlink traversal undermines configured local-root containment for file-writing tools.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: General MCP filesystem server catalog context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General local agent file-boundary practice is development-practice-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Owns the symlink traversal and local-root containment failure.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD for date and affected boundary; ingest should verify whether a patched version exists.
follow_up_actions: Check Traceforce and project releases for fixed version.
Compare with existing filesystem/path traversal MCP leaves to avoid duplicate synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: VoiceMode MCP update_config command injection
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD reports that VoiceMode through 8.10.1 writes caller-supplied MCP update_config values into ~/.voicemode/voicemode.env without shell-safe escaping, creating OS command-injection risk. References include a v8.10.2 release and fixing commit.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database with release and commit references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: VoiceMode <= 8.10.1; update_config MCP tool and voicemode config set CLI
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Configuration tools for voice or agent runtimes can become command-execution paths when caller-controlled values cross into shell-loaded environment files.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: General VoiceMode product or voice-agent context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General local runtime configuration practice is development-practice-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Owns the MCP configuration command-injection boundary and fixed-version note.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD and linked release/commit; verify v8.10.2 release notes during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Create or update a local MCP command-injection leaf if not already represented.
Record v8.10.2 as the apparent patched release after direct release verification.

qualifying_findings.title: MetaMCP session IDOR and stdio inspector proxy code execution
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD reports two MetaMCP issues through 2.4.22: session dispatch keyed only by client-supplied mcp-session-id without owner or endpoint binding, allowing cross-tenant private tool execution and data exfiltration, and code execution in the internal MCP inspector proxy endpoint GET /mcp-proxy/server/stdio.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database with project and security advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MetaMCP through 2.4.22; MCP transport session dispatch and internal inspector stdio proxy
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MetaMCP is an aggregator/control-plane style MCP surface; tenant binding failures and proxy code execution can compromise private tools, forwarded credentials, and local execution boundaries.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: General MetaMCP product catalog context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General MCP aggregation/control-plane practice is development-practice-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Owns tenant session isolation, credential forwarding, and proxy code-execution implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for paired same-version boundary from NVD; fixed-version status was not visible in captured data.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, decide whether to split IDOR and code execution into separate leaves or one tightly coupled MetaMCP control-plane cluster.
Recheck project advisory or releases for patched version.

qualifying_findings.title: Open GenAI Stack prompt injection to Jinja server-side expression evaluation
qualifying_findings.summary: NVD reports that Open GenAI Stack, also named ogx-ai and described as used in the Meta AI backend for WhatsApp and other products, permits code execution because prompt injection using Jinja2 template syntax can reach unsanitized server-side expression evaluation.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database with public technical gist reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Open GenAI Stack / ogx-ai 2026-06-11; prompt-to-template evaluation path
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a model/prompt security boundary crossing into server-side execution, showing prompt content becoming executable template syntax in an AI backend path.

qualifying_findings.title: Frontier AI voluntary accord adds internal controls, external auditors, and board review
qualifying_findings.summary: Associated Press reported that President Trump and leaders from major AI companies signed a voluntary accord focused on self-policing frontier AI development. The reported steps include robust internal controls, independent external auditor assessment, and a board committee review of internal and external auditor reports.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: reputable public news report; primary signed accord text not directly fetched in this run
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Frontier AI governance and assurance controls; voluntary accord covering named signatories reported by AP
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Internal controls, external audits, and board-level review are release-gate and assurance mechanisms for frontier AI risks, even though the accord is voluntary and not itself a binding regulatory rule.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad company and federal AI policy context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General governance process practice is development-practice-owned where it affects software delivery.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Owns the assurance-control and release-gate implication for AI security risk management.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium confidence because AP is reputable and the article says the accord was posted on Truth Social, but this run did not locate a stable primary accord URL.
